headline: Margins compress on tariffs, but easy comp lifts earnings
summary_short: Net sales fell 4% year over year to $2.37 billion as tariffs and cost inflation cut gross margin 190bp to 27.5%, while EPS of $0.41 more than doubled year over year against an easy comparison to last year's $150 million trademark impairment.
summary_long: Third-quarter net sales fell 4% year over year to $2.37 billion on unfavorable volume/mix and the Noosa divestiture, partly offset by favorable pricing. Gross margin fell 190bp to 27.5% as tariffs (an estimated 310bp drag) and input-cost inflation outweighed productivity gains and pricing. Segment operating earnings fell 22% to $308 million on lower gross profit in both Meals & Beverages and Snacks. Net earnings of $124 million ($0.41 diluted) roughly doubled year over year, but the comparison was easy: the prior-year quarter carried a $150 million Snyder's of Hanover trademark impairment. Cost-savings and optimization charges totaled $69 million this quarter. Cash and equivalents ended the quarter at $402 million, up from $132 million at fiscal year start.

drivers.explanation: Unfavorable volume/mix and the noosa divestiture drove the decline, partly offset by favorable net pricing. By segment: Meals & Beverages fell on U.S. soup declines and Rao's shipment timing tied to a prior-year SAP rollout; Snacks fell on crackers, pretzels, third-party brands and contract manufacturing.
Margin fell 190bp to 27.5% as tariffs (an estimated 310bp drag), cost inflation and other supply-chain costs outweighed supply-chain productivity gains and favorable pricing.

EBIT improved sharply because last year's quarter absorbed a $150 million Snyder's of Hanover trademark impairment; this year included $30 million of pension actuarial and curtailment gains, per the filing's own EBIT line of $239 million versus $161 million a year ago.

Net earnings roughly doubled to $124 million from $66 million as items impacting comparability swung from a $152 million EPS drag last year (mostly the Snyder's impairment) to just a $26 million drag this year.
Diluted EPS of $0.41 included $0.09 of expense from items impacting comparability, versus $0.51 of such expense a year ago (mainly the trademark impairment), which explains most of the y/y increase.

Management cited persistent tariff and input-cost inflation pressuring margins through the rest of fiscal 2026, with cost-savings initiatives and pricing needed to offset; consumer volumes are expected to stay pressured by economic uncertainty.
